story.iWant: to sign in using my social media account (Google, GitHub, etc.)
story.soThat: I can access the platform quickly without creating a separate password

tasks.task: Configure OAuth providers in NextAuth.js (AC: #1, #4) - Install required NextAuth.js OAuth provider packages (Google, GitHub) - Add Google OAuth provider to NextAuth.js configuration in `src/lib/auth.ts` - Add GitHub OAuth provider to NextAuth.js configuration (optional) - Configure OAuth callback URLs for each provider - Set up environment variables for OAuth client IDs and secrets - Implement PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for enhanced security - Configure OAuth scopes: request only email and profile (minimum necessary permissions) - Test: Verify OAuth providers are properly configured - Test: Verify PKCE flow works correctly - Test: Verify OAuth state parameter validation prevents CSRF

Implement OAuth account linking logic (AC: #1, #3) - Create account linking service in `src/lib/auth/oauth-linking.ts` - Implement email matching logic: if OAuth email matches existing account, link accounts - Implement account creation logic: if email doesn't exist, create new account - Store OAuth provider ID and encrypted access token in database - Support multiple OAuth providers per user (link Google and GitHub to same account) - Update Prisma schema if needed to support OAuth account linking (add account table or extend user table) - Test: Verify account linking works for existing users - Test: Verify new account creation works for new users - Test: Verify multiple OAuth providers can be linked to same account

Create OAuth authentication buttons component (AC: #2) - Create `src/components/auth/OAuthButtons.tsx` component - Use NextAuth.js `signIn()` function with provider ID - Display provider icons (Google logo, GitHub logo) using Icon component - Style buttons to match design system (Competitive Data theme colors) - Implement loading state during OAuth flow (button disabled, spinner shown) - Ensure buttons are accessible (keyboard navigation, ARIA labels) - Add "Sign in with Google" and "Sign in with GitHub" buttons - Test: Verify buttons render correctly on login and signup pages - Test: Verify buttons are accessible via keyboard - Test: Verify loading states work correctly

Add OAuth buttons to login and signup pages (AC: #2) - Update `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` to include OAuth buttons - Update `src/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx` to include OAuth buttons - Add visual separator ("or" divider) between OAuth buttons and email/password form - Ensure responsive layout works at all breakpoints (320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px) - Test: Verify OAuth buttons appear on login page - Test: Verify OAuth buttons appear on signup page - Test: Verify responsive layout works correctly

Implement OAuth error handling (AC: #1) - Create error mapping for OAuth provider errors - Handle OAuth callback errors (access denied, invalid state, etc.) - Display user-friendly error messages for OAuth failures - Log OAuth errors to security_events table for monitoring - Redirect to error page with clear error message if OAuth fails - Test: Verify error handling works for all OAuth error scenarios - Test: Verify error messages are user-friendly - Test: Verify OAuth errors are logged correctly

Implement OAuth session management (AC: #1) - Configure NextAuth.js callbacks to handle OAuth user data - Map OAuth provider user data to NextAuth session - Store OAuth provider information in session (for account linking display) - Implement token refresh for OAuth providers that support it - Ensure OAuth sessions work with existing session management infrastructure - Test: Verify OAuth sessions are created correctly - Test: Verify OAuth sessions persist across browser tabs - Test: Verify token refresh works for OAuth providers

Security and audit logging (AC: #4) - Log OAuth authentication events to security_events table - Log account linking events (when OAuth account is linked to existing user) - Implement OAuth state parameter validation to prevent CSRF - Encrypt OAuth access tokens before storing in database - Test: Verify OAuth events are logged correctly - Test: Verify CSRF protection works (state parameter validation) - Test: Verify OAuth tokens are encrypted in database

Accessibility and responsive design compliance (AC: #2) - Ensure OAuth buttons meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance - Add proper ARIA labels to OAuth buttons - Verify keyboard navigation works correctly - Test screen reader compatibility - Ensure responsive design works at all breakpoints (320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px) - Test: Verify accessibility compliance using @axe-core/playwright - Test: Verify responsive design on real devices

criteria.given: I am on the registration or login page
criteria.when: I click a social authentication button (e.g., "Sign in with Google")
criteria.then: - Redirects to OAuth provider authorization page - Requests minimum necessary permissions (email, profile) - After user authorizes, receives OAuth callback with authorization code - Exchanges code for access token and user profile information - Creates account if email doesn't exist, or links to existing account if email matches - Creates secure session and redirects to dashboard - Handles OAuth provider errors gracefully with user-friendly error messages

criteria.given: The social authentication buttons are displayed
criteria.then: - Display provider icons (Google logo, GitHub logo, etc.) - Have consistent styling matching the design system - Show loading state during OAuth flow - Are accessible via keyboard navigation

- If email from OAuth provider matches existing account, link OAuth account to existing user - If email doesn't exist, create new account with OAuth provider information - Store OAuth provider ID and access token (encrypted) for future authentication - Support multiple OAuth providers per user (user can link Google and GitHub to same account)

- Use Authorization Code flow with PKCE for enhanced security - Validate OAuth state parameter to prevent CSRF attacks - Store OAuth tokens securely (encrypted in database) - Implement token refresh for long-lived sessions - Log OAuth authentication events to security_events table

docs.doc: FR1: Users can create accounts with email or social authentication. Includes requirements for OAuth providers and account linking.

NextAuth.js 4.24.12 for authentication handling and session management. Supports OAuth providers. Cookie-based sessions with secure HTTP-only cookies. JWT strategy with 7-day expiration, refresh token rotation with 30-day expiration.
Prisma ORM 5.0.0 for type-safe database access. PostgreSQL via Supabase. User model defined in prisma/schema.prisma. May need Account model or extended User model for OAuth account linking.

Complete story definition with acceptance criteria and technical notes. Use NextAuth.js OAuth providers configuration. Supported providers: Google (required), GitHub (optional). OAuth flow: Authorization Code flow with PKCE for security. Account linking: Match by email address, create if new, link if existing.
ShadCN/UI (New York style) components configured with Competitive Data theme. Button components with consistent styling. CSS variables for theming (Deep Indigo #4f46e5, Cyan #06b6d4, Purple #8b5cf6).
Mobile-first approach with breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px. Touch-optimized interactions for mobile devices.
WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance required. Keyboard navigation support. Screen reader compatibility. Color contrast ratios meet WCAG standards (minimum 4.5:1).

Auth infrastructure available: NextAuth.js configured with CredentialsProvider using Supabase Auth. Session management helpers available at `src/lib/auth/nextauth-helpers.ts`. Use existing authentication infrastructure.

Validation utilities: Email validation schemas available at `src/lib/auth/validation.ts` with RFC 5322 email validation. Form components: ShadCN/UI Form components with react-hook-form integration already established. Icon system: Icon wrapper component available at `src/components/ui/icon.tsx` for consistent Lucide React usage. Error handling: Error mapping service available for user-friendly error messages.
Design system available with CSS variables, ShadCN/UI components, icon system, responsive utilities, animation system, accessibility testing framework established.

constraints.constraint: Use NextAuth.js 4.24.12 for OAuth provider configuration and session management
OAuth flow: Authorization Code flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for enhanced security
OAuth providers: Google (required), GitHub (optional), others as needed
OAuth scopes: Request only email and profile (minimum necessary permissions)
Account linking: Match by email address, create new account if email doesn't exist, link to existing account if email matches
Support multiple OAuth providers per user (user can link Google and GitHub to same account)
Store OAuth provider ID and encrypted access token in database
Implement OAuth state parameter validation to prevent CSRF attacks
Log OAuth authentication events to security_events table for audit trail
Use ShadCN/UI Button components with design system styling for OAuth buttons
Use Icon component from `src/components/ui/icon.tsx` for provider icons (may need to add Google/GitHub icons or use SVG)
Mobile-first responsive design with breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px
WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance required, minimum 4.5:1 color contrast ratio for text
Implement custom error mapping for OAuth provider errors with user-friendly messages
Follow design system: Competitive Data theme colors (Deep Indigo #4f46e5, Cyan #06b6d4, Purple #8b5cf6)
Component location: Auth components in src/components/auth/ directory
API routes: OAuth callbacks handled automatically by NextAuth.js via /api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts
Auth utilities: Authentication utilities in src/lib/auth/ directory
Maintain 80%+ test coverage with unit, integration, and E2E tests
Follow TDD approach (Red-Green-Refactor cycle) - write tests before implementation
Use @axe-core/playwright for E2E accessibility testing
Session strategy: JWT with refresh token rotation, session expires 7 days, refresh token expires 30 days
